label_notes: SELF-RAG introduces reflection-token-based adaptive retrieval and self-critique for retrieval-augmented generation. Core innovations include Retrieve, ISREL, ISSUP, and ISUSE tokens integrated directly into LM generation. Metrics are grounded in Table 2 and Figures 3–4. The framework trains a critic model offline using GPT-4-generated supervision and then trains a generator LM to jointly generate outputs and reflection tokens. SELF-RAG significantly improves factuality, citation precision, and controllability over standard RAG baselines and retrieval-augmented ChatGPT systems.

qa_cases.question: What is HyDE in dense retrieval?
Why does HyDE improve zero-shot retrieval?
How is HyDE different from Contriever-only retrieval?

label_notes: HyDE reframes zero-shot dense retrieval as a two-stage pipeline: generate a hypothetical relevant document with an instruction-following LLM, then encode it using an unsupervised contrastive encoder like Contriever. The generated document may hallucinate details, but the dense embedding bottleneck filters irrelevant information. HyDE requires no relevance labels or retraining and substantially improves zero-shot retrieval performance across web search, fact verification, QA, and multilingual retrieval tasks. The paper positions HyDE as a bridge between LLM generation and dense retrieval.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

qa_cases.question: What is the Lost in the Middle effect in long-context LLMs?

What are the implications of Lost in the Middle for RAG systems?

label_notes: This paper introduces a systematic evaluation protocol for measuring how language models use long input contexts. The authors demonstrate a strong U-shaped performance curve where models perform best when relevant information appears at the beginning or end of context windows and significantly worse when relevant information appears in the middle. The study evaluates both multi-document QA and synthetic key-value retrieval across open and closed models, showing that larger context windows do not necessarily imply robust long-context reasoning. The findings have major implications for RAG pipelines, retrieval ordering, and long-context benchmark design.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

limitations_stated: performance depends heavily on function-calling reliability

qa_cases.question: How does MemGPT emulate virtual memory for LLMs?

label_notes: MemGPT introduces an operating-system-inspired architecture for extending the effective context length of large language models through hierarchical memory management. Instead of relying only on larger context windows, MemGPT treats the prompt as constrained RAM and enables the model to autonomously move information between working memory and external storage via function calls. The system includes archival storage, recall storage, queue management, recursive summarization, and event-driven control flow. Experiments show strong gains in long-term conversational consistency, document QA, and nested multi-hop retrieval tasks compared to fixed-context baselines.

label_notes: This paper introduced chain-of-thought prompting, where few-shot exemplars include intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer. The work demonstrated that sufficiently large language models exhibit emergent reasoning abilities when prompted with natural language reasoning traces. Major gains were shown on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks, especially GSM8K. The paper established chain-of-thought prompting as a foundational reasoning technique later extended by self-consistency, ReAct, Tree-of-Thoughts, Reflexion, and agentic planning systems.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

expected_readiness.min_gpu_requirement: 6B-7B parameter class models for meaningful tool learning

qa_cases.question: How does Toolformer learn to use APIs?

label_notes: Toolformer introduced a self-supervised framework where language models learn to call external APIs without explicit human supervision. The system samples candidate API calls, executes them, filters useful calls based on whether they reduce perplexity for future token prediction, and finetunes the model on successful examples. Toolformer demonstrated substantial gains on reasoning, factual QA, arithmetic, multilingual QA, and temporal reasoning tasks using tools such as calculators, QA systems, Wikipedia search, translation systems, and calendars. The paper became foundational for modern tool-calling and agentic LLM architectures.

label_notes: SWE-agent introduced the concept of Agent-Computer Interfaces (ACIs) for software engineering agents. Instead of exposing a raw Linux shell, SWE-agent provides LM-friendly abstractions for repository navigation, editing, search, and execution. The interface includes summarized search commands, interactive file viewers, line-based editing, syntax-aware guardrails, and context management mechanisms. The paper demonstrated major gains over shell-only and RAG baselines on SWE-bench and established a foundational paradigm for autonomous software engineering agents and coding copilots.

label_notes: WebArena introduced one of the first highly realistic, reproducible, fully interactive web environments for evaluating autonomous agents on long-horizon browser tasks. The benchmark combines self-hosted websites from multiple real-world domains with outcome-based functional evaluation rather than action-sequence matching. The paper highlighted the large gap between human and GPT-4 performance and established WebArena as a foundational benchmark for browser agents, web navigation systems, ReAct-style planning agents, and autonomous digital workers.

label_notes: AutoGen became one of the foundational frameworks for production-oriented LLM multi-agent systems. The paper introduced the concepts of conversable agents and conversation programming, where agent orchestration is modeled as message-driven computation and control flow. AutoGen demonstrated that LLMs, tools, and humans can be composed into reusable agent abstractions supporting dynamic workflows, tool usage, code execution, group chat, and human oversight. The framework strongly influenced later orchestration systems such as LangGraph-based agents, autonomous coding agents, MCP ecosystems, and enterprise multi-agent architectures.

label_notes: VOYAGER introduced one of the first successful lifelong embodied LLM agents capable of autonomous exploration and skill accumulation in Minecraft. The system combines an automatic curriculum, executable skill library, and iterative prompting mechanism using GPT-4 as a blackbox planner. Instead of low-level actions, VOYAGER uses executable code as the action space, enabling compositional long-horizon behaviors. The paper demonstrated major gains over ReAct, Reflexion, and AutoGPT baselines in exploration, tech tree mastery, map traversal, and zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks.

qa_cases.question: What is the primary contribution of Reflexion?
How does Reflexion use memory and verbal feedback across trials?
What headline HumanEval result is reported for Reflexion with GPT-4?

label_notes: Reflexion introduced one of the foundational architectures for self-improving LLM agents through verbal reinforcement learning. Instead of updating model weights, Reflexion stores natural-language reflections from failed trajectories into episodic memory and reuses them in future attempts. The architecture separates the system into Actor, Evaluator, and Self-Reflection models. The paper demonstrated strong gains across ALFWorld, HotPotQA, HumanEval, MBPP, and LeetcodeHardGym, including a major jump from GPT-4's 80.1% to 91% pass@1 on HumanEval Python. Reflexion became one of the core conceptual building blocks behind modern retry/self-correction agent architectures, reflection loops, evaluator-guided agents, and memory-augmented orchestration systems.

limitations_stated: beam search integration not fully explored

qa_cases.question: What is the primary contribution of speculative decoding?
How does speculative decoding use a draft model and target model?
What headline speedups are reported for speculative decoding on translation and summarization?

label_notes: Speculative Decoding introduced the foundational draft-and-verify decoding paradigm now widely adopted in modern LLM inference systems. The method uses a smaller approximation model to draft several tokens ahead, then verifies them in parallel with the larger target model while preserving the exact output distribution. The paper formalized speculative sampling, acceptance-rate analysis, and walltime/speedup equations. It demonstrated practical 2x-3x inference acceleration on T5-XXL and strong acceptance rates across GPT-like and LaMDA models without retraining or architecture changes. This work became one of the core inference optimization techniques used in production LLM serving stacks.

label_notes: Graph of Thoughts generalizes Chain-of-Thought and Tree-of-Thought prompting by representing reasoning as arbitrary graphs instead of chains or trees. The framework introduces graph-enabled thought transformations such as aggregation and refinement, enabling richer reasoning structures and improved performance on complex decomposition-heavy tasks like sorting, set operations, keyword counting, and document merging.
